The Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria says it identified between 40 and 50 suspected examination impersonators during its recently concluded Professional Qualifying Examination. The Registrar/Chief Executive of TRCN, Dr Ronke Soyombo, disclosed this in an interview with the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Sunday in Abuja. Soyombo said the council identified the suspected impersonators through the introduction of candidates’ photographs into the examination process. She described the innovation as a significant improvement in examination security and efforts to eliminate impersonation among candidates. “For instance, in one state, we were able to identify approximately 40 to 50 individuals who were attempting to impersonate registered candidates,” she said. The registrar, however, acknowledged that the examination encountered technical challenges, particularly poor internet connectivity in Ogun and Kaduna states. According to her, the exercise was successful in 35 locations, but inadequate bandwidth affected the stability of the examination platform in Ogun and Kaduna. Soyombo explained that the council had initially secured a well-equipped Computer-Based Test centre in Ogun but encountered difficulties when the facility was declared unavailable. She said TRCN had to secure an alternative centre within 24 hours, but its capacity was inadequate for approximately 1,000 candidates. On efforts to increase teacher registration, Soyombo said the council’s digital platform had significantly improved registration and examination participation. She said applications increased from approximately 13,000 when she assumed office in May 2025 to 26,000 by November 2025. She added that approximately 21,000 teachers sat for the November 2026 Professional Qualifying Examination nationwide. Soyombo said the Federal Government had set a target of registering 75 per cent of teachers by the end of the year. She also disclosed that the government had introduced a six-month Accelerated Teacher Professionalisation Pathway targeting 250,000 teachers, with the first cohort comprising 50,000 participants. According to her, the programme combines four months of lectures with two months of supervised teaching practice, leading to a Postgraduate Diploma in Education (PGDE) qualification.
